identity.title: The Physical Conditions in a Pre-super Star Cluster Molecular Cloud in the Antennae Galaxies

paper_type_evidence.quote: We have obtained ALMA CO and 870$\mu$m observations of the Antennae galaxy system with $\sim 0''.5$ resolution.

targets.name: Compact cloud in SGMC2, Antennae overlap region

evidence.quote: adopting a distance of 21.5 Mpc
adopting a distance of 21.5 Mpc

question.value: What are the physical conditions (size, mass, temperature, pressure) of a compact massive molecular cloud in the Antennae, and can it form a globular cluster / super star cluster?

evidence.quote: The present paper characterizes this source, which we consider among the best candidates for a proto-SSC, and lays out the evidence for and against the source’s eventual evolution into a SSC or GC.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data : ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00876.S.

bands.value: CO(3-2) and 870 um continuum (Cycle 0); SV CO(2-1)

evidence.quote: We obtained ALMA observations of the Antennae system in CO(3-2) and 870$\;\mu$m continuum
in CO(3-2) and 870$\;\mu$m continuum
The SV CO(2-1) data used in this paper was taken with a beam size of $1.68''\times 0.85''$.
the observations consisted of a 13-point mosaic, and were carried out in the “extended” configuration

with a maximum baseline of $\sim
400$ m and 5 km s$^{-1}$ spectral channels

With an angular resolution FWHM of $0.''56 \times 0.''43$ ($59 \times
45$ pc)
The largest angular scale to which the CO(3-2) observations are sensitive is $\sim 6''$

sensitivity.value: rms 3.3 mJy/beam (CO 3-2, 5 km/s channels); SV CO(2-1) 6.5 mJy/beam

evidence.quote: The resulting rms was determined using line-free channels and found to be 3.3 mJy/beam.

provided.value: Radio maps constraining free-free emission / ionizing flux

evidence.quote: We created two radio maps from archival 3.6 cm VLA observations (proposal codes AN079, AP478, AS796, AA301)

evidence.quote: We also register the astrometry of archival Hubble Space Telescope observations

evidence.quote:
Assuming a dust emissivity of $\kappa = 0.9
\pm 0.13$ cm$^{2}$ g$^{-1}$ (cite: wilson08)

analysis_steps.goal: Extract cloud and measure size/line width

method.value: Sub-cube ~1''x1''x300 km/s, Gaussian fits and deconvolution of beam; cross-checked with CPROPS

evidence.quote: We extract the primary cloud from the velocity cube for further analysis by creating a sub-cube around the cloud with dimensions of $\sim 1''\times 1'' \times 300$ km s$^{-1}$.

validation.value: CPROPS on whole cube agrees within uncertainties

evidence.quote: the resulting parameters agree to within the uncertainties

method.value: RADEX grid of CO(3-2) and CO(2-1) intensities, chi-squared minimization

evidence.quote: The best-fit values result from a chi-squared minimization.

key_parameters.value: CO(3-2) filling fraction 1; CO(2-1) set to dilution factor

evidence.quote: for CO(3-2) we set the beam filling fraction to 1, and for CO(2-1) we set it to the dilution factor

evidence.loc: Results, Cloud Temperature and Optical Depth
evidence.quote: The line intensities and their ratio were compared to a grid of RADEX models covering a range of values for kinetic temperature, CO column density, and H$_2$ volume density.

method.value: Virial (isothermal sphere), RADEX column density, XCO, 870um dust continuum

evidence.quote: The mass of the cloud is estimated using four different methods, each subject to different caveats.

evidence.quote: gas-to-dust ratio of 120$\pm 28$, and dust temperature of 20 K

validation.value: Compared methods; virial treated as upper limit, RADEX as lower limit

evidence.quote: we treat the estimated virial mass as an *upper* limit.

findings_qualitative.value: No thermal radio or Paα source is associated with the cloud, so star formation has not yet altered it.

evidence.quote: the lack of associated thermal radio emission indicates that star formation has not yet altered the environment

claims.hypothesis: Is the cloud a pre-SSC capable of forming a globular cluster?
claims.experiment: CO(3-2) size/mass, continuum mass, radio/Paα limits
claims.result: Radius <=24 pc, mass ~0.3-1.5e7 Msun, no ionizing source

evidence.quote: The cloud appears capable of forming a globular cluster

claims.hypothesis: Does confinement require high external pressure?

evidence.quote:
it must be subject to an external pressure of P/$k_B \gtrsim
  10^8$ K cm$^{-3}$

limitations_admitted.value: Cloud only marginally resolved; temperature-density degeneracy; mass methods have different caveats.

evidence.quote: there is a degeneracy between the inferred temperature and density of the cloud

referee_caveats_inferred: Single marginally resolved cloud; size is an upper limit
Large mass spread between methods; virial mass 5-10x too high
